title: ASCII Kinesis V2 Locomotion 025 — Low Obstacle Split Support / Trailing Clearance Runout

source.identity: Bob — Bob the Builder: Fix It Fun! — Game Boy / GBC — Playable Characters
observed: The commissioned evidence explicitly treated the entire 506×428 sheet as one whole-sheet image rather than an isolated sprite.
The source exposes ten named families including side-travel Walk/Run plus Duck, Climb, Off Ladder, Push and Pick Item.
Side-travel families visibly include narrower and wider stride organizations, while frontal/vertical-support states reorganize limbs around a centered root.
No source-authentic exposure duration was measured from the static sheet or preview animations.
unknown: Source-authentic chronology, exposure duration, exact root path, obstacle-step choreography, foot-clearance arc, support forces, and gameplay cadence are unknown.

rights.output_description: independent generic ASCII biped/root-support rig crossing an abstract low obstacle

novelty.new_causality: Continuous forward travel crosses a low fixed obstacle without becoming a jump or crouch gait. The lead foot clears and earns fixed support beyond the obstacle while the rear foot still owns ground behind it, creating a brief split-support bridge across the obstacle. Root/COM then pass through that support gap before the trailing foot releases, rises late, clears the obstacle, and lands in an intentionally overlong catch. Shorter corrections pay surviving forward and clearance debt without an idle reset.
failure_if: lead foot contacts the obstacle instead of clearing before support acquisition
lead support teleports beyond the obstacle without a visible clearance arc
root stops at the obstacle instead of traversing the split-support bridge
trailing foot clips the obstacle or releases before lead support is trustworthy
the trailing-foot catch is not visibly overlong
post-catch root spacing does not shorten
recovery returns to the approach pose or erases secondary lag

timing.playback_policy: authored decisive causal keys with explicit holds; support topology changes and obstacle-clearance extrema are authored keys; no reverse interpolation

rig.support_rule: A foot is trusted only in PLANTED_FIXED or UNLOADING_FIXED. The lead foot must visibly clear the obstacle before its beyond-obstacle catch can own the root; the trailing foot may release only after that support is earned.
rig.clearance_rule: No authored foot center enters the obstacle box x=[236,278], y=[264,290]. Lead and trailing feet each have authored above-top clearance keys before crossing the far edge.
rig.bridge_rule: K04 establishes split support across the obstacle: old left support behind, new right support beyond. K05-K07 carry root/COM through that bridge while trailing left foot releases and clears.
rig.runout_rule: K08 is the largest root-spacing event after trailing clearance; K09-K12 shorten 27→18→13→9 px while settle remains displaced.
rig.secondary_rule: Torso lean and free-foot lag peak around the late trailing clearance/catch and decay through corrections without returning to the approach pose.

keys.name: OBSTACLE_READ_SHORTEN
keys.causal_role: shorten and lower slightly before the obstacle rather than converting the event into a jump

keys.name: LEAD_KNEE_LIFT
keys.causal_role: lift the lead right foot above obstacle height while old left support remains fixed and root travel stays live

keys.name: LEAD_TOE_CLEAR_FRONT_EDGE
keys.causal_role: carry the lead foot across the obstacle top on an authored high point before any new support claim

keys.name: LEAD_CATCH_BEYOND_SPLIT_SUPPORT
keys.causal_role: earn right-foot support beyond the obstacle while rear left support is still behind, creating the split-support bridge

keys.name: ROOT_ENTERS_SUPPORT_GAP
keys.causal_role: release the trailing left foot only after right support is trustworthy and carry root/COM toward the obstacle gap

keys.name: ROOT_PASSES_TRAIL_TOE_CLEAR
keys.causal_role: let root/COM pass the obstacle as the trailing toe clears the far edge; support ownership does not teleport

keys.name: TRAILING_FREE_CATCH_OVERRUN
keys.causal_role: preserve surviving forward velocity into an intentionally overlong trailing-foot catch far beyond the obstacle; the old right support unloads behind a visibly stretched recovery stance

keys.name: LEFT_BRAKE_COMPRESSION
keys.causal_role: hold the exaggerated left catch world-fixed and compress beneath it to brake translation while the free right side and torso remain late

keys.name: RIGHT_SHORT_COUNTERCATCH
keys.causal_role: use a shorter right countercatch behind the prior free-foot reach to absorb remaining debt without becoming a symmetric gait phase

keys.name: LEFT_CORRECTION_PROBE
keys.causal_role: advance a still-smaller left probe while right support stays trustworthy and secondary lag continues to decay

keys.name: DISPLACED_RECOVERY_SETTLE
keys.causal_role: settle beyond the obstacle with residual forward intent and free-foot debt rather than returning to the approach pose

quality_history.highest_value_visible_defect: K08 post-clearance catch read too close to a tidy two-foot restack; the overrun debt was numerically large in root spacing but not emphatic enough in the landing silhouette.
quality_history.concrete_correction: On SAME Locomotion025, push K08 trailing left catch farther forward while keeping the old right foot unloading behind it; then retune K09-K12 as progressively shorter root/support corrections so the catch debt is visible before it is paid.

quality_history.verdict: Lead foot visibly clears before K04 establishes split support across the obstacle; root/COM continue through the support gap while the trailing foot releases late and clears at K06-K07. R1 K08 now lands as a stretched overlong catch rather than a tidy restack, and K09-K12 visibly compress 29.8→20.4→14.3→10.4 px while residual torso/free-side lag decays without idle reset. No support teleport, obstacle clip, equal-spacing gait, straight endpoint tween, reverse interpolation, or metadata-only clearance survives.

The obstacle is not scenery: it forces two different clearance events, an earned split-support bridge, a late trailing release, and a rude long catch before the corrections shrink. Silhouette progression is specific and economical, with enough remaining imbalance to avoid a showroom reset.
